extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent prosecution examiners reviewing written description/benefit claims)
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO training workshop for examiners on applying 35 U.S.C. 112(a) written description requirements (including 112(f) / means-plus-function, provisional benefit claims, enablement distinctions, and sample office action language) to computer- and hardware-related patent claims. Uses a facial-recognition hypothetical to practice claim construction, support analysis, and drafting of rejections/notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) of the claim (consider 112(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the broadest reasonable interpretation of each claim; remember to consider whether the claims invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BRI step includes checking whether claim terms (e.g., 'unit') are generic placeholders that trigger 112(f). If 112(f) applies, interpret the limitation to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents. (See MPEP 2181.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification as filed must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail so that one of ordinary skill in the art can reasonably conclude that the inventor had possession of the claimed invention at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure only restates functional language or uses generic placeholders without sufficient structural detail, it may fail 112(a). Use Form Paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.31.01 for rejections. Example: generic 'capturing unit' or 'analyzing unit' without structure is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(f)/means-plus-function invocation and corresponding structure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim uses 'means' or a substitute (e.g., 'unit') that is a generic placeholder modified by functional language and lacks sufficiently definite structure, it invokes 35 U.S.C. 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such claim elements must be interpreted to cover the corresponding structure, materials, or acts described in the specification and 'equivalents thereof.' If the specification does not disclose corresponding structure, those limitations lack written description support and may be indefinite under 112(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-implemented functional limitations require algorithmic/corresponding structure disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer-implemented specialized functions recited functionally, the disclosure must include corresponding structure — i.e., a general purpose computer or component plus the algorithms that perform the claimed functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely asserting that one of ordinary skill could devise an algorithm is insufficient for written description. Flowcharts or generic unit names without algorithms or instruction-level disclosure may fail to demonstrate possession. If missing, claim may also be indefinite under 112(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze written description support in the earlier (provisional) application for benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a later application claims benefit of an earlier filing date, evaluate whether the earlier-filed application provides adequate 112(a) support for each claim limitation that purports to receive the earlier date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier disclosure is sparse (e.g., generic 'units' without structure), claims in the later application are not entitled to the earlier filing date. Examiner should notify applicant that benefit is not proper (use Form Paragraphs 2.09 and 2.10) and perform prior art search based on the actual filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze written description support in the non-provisional specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether the non-provisional specification provides sufficient structure, embodiments, or detail to support each claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-provisional disclosure that identifies concrete structure (e.g., a digital camera, CPU programmed with APIDQ instructions, specific network interface) can provide 112(a) support and satisfy corresponding-structure requirements for 112(f) elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim scope must be commensurate with the disclosure (numerical ranges and broad genus claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim limitations (including numerical ranges like 'at least 90%') must be supported by the specification; the claim's BRI determines its scope (e.g., 'at least 90%' reads up to 100%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification only shows up to 97%, a claim covering up to 100% lacks written description support and should be rejected under 112(a). Consider narrowing or limiting to disclosed species to remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments that introduce new technical matter are improper (new matter prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that add specifics not present in the original disclosure (e.g., adding 'Gaussian high pass filter' when not originally disclosed) constitute new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments lack written description support and add new matter; reject under 112(a) and advise applicant. Use sample rejection language; recommend applicant may change application relationship to CIP or delete benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural claim terms versus functional placeholders (impact on 112(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms that recite sufficiently definite structure (e.g., 'filter') generally do not invoke 112(f), whereas generic placeholders like 'unit' often do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a term is structural, claim is not limited to the corresponding structure in the specification and covers all appropriate equivalents; nonetheless, written description support is still required to show possession of the claimed structural function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when later-filed claims are not entitled to earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are not supported by the earlier filing, the examiner should notify applicant and proceed based on the actual filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify using form paragraphs (e.g., 2.09, 2.10), perform prior-art search as of actual filing date, and may use intervening references in rejections until applicant corrects the benefit claim or shows entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for evaluating the propriety of a benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate entitlement to an earlier filing date when there is a reason to question the adequacy of support in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical triggers include an intervening prior art reference, significant broadening of later-filed claims, or when the earlier application appears substantially less substantial than the later-filed application. Best practice: verify benefit claim when such circumstances arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MPEP and form paragraphs as procedural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply relevant MPEP sections (e.g., 2161-2163, 2181, 211.05) and use recommended form paragraphs for notifications and rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample language is provided for notifying lack of benefit (Form Paragraphs 2.09/2.10) and for written description rejections (Form Paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.31.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish written description, enablement, and indefiniteness analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Written description concerns possession; enablement concerns ability to make and use without undue experimentation (Wands factors); indefiniteness under 112(b) can arise when functional claim elements lack corresponding structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to discuss enablement issues raised by Wands factors though this workshop focuses on written description. Example: the specification may be enabling (one of ordinary skill could implement) but still fail written description if inventor did not show possession of the full claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments may remove 112(f) invocation but can broaden scope and create written description problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding structural language (e.g., specifying a 'central processing unit having a memory with instructions stored therein') can avoid 112(f) but may broaden claim to cover all ways of performing the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification only discloses a particular species (e.g., APIDQ) and indicates that species is critical, the broader amended claim may still lack written description support. Remedy: limit the claim to the disclosed species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original claims do not automatically provide written description support for themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely reproducing a claim limitation in the specification or pointing to an original claim does not necessarily satisfy written description unless the claim itself conveys sufficient information to show possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate on a case-by-case basis; do not assume that an original claim, by its wording, constitutes adequate written description of structural detail or algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative terms (e.g., 'about') are judged in context for definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of relative terms like 'about' does not automatically render a claim indefinite; context and the state of the art determine whether the term is definite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider specification examples and state of the art (see MPEP 2173.05(B)(II)). In the example, 'about a 95% accurate image detection rate' is sufficiently definite to be allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(f) limitations unsupported by corresponding structure may render claim indefinite under 112(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a functionally claimed element invokes 112(f) but the specification lacks corresponding structure, the limitation may be both unsupported under 112(a) and indefinite under 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check for both written description and definiteness problems and cite appropriate MPEP guidance and prior training where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession for software-related inventions requires disclosure of how functions are performed
rubrics_metrics.description: For software-related inventions, describing only the function/result is often insufficient; the specification should identify how the inventor devised the function (algorithms/instructions) to show possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/anti-patterns: stating that an analyzing unit 'analyzes pixel values' without algorithmic detail is inadequate. Disclose APIs, algorithms, flowchart steps with sufficient detail as appropriate for the technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent-claim limitations can cure broad independent-claim deficiencies if limited to disclosed species
rubrics_metrics.description: Limiting dependent claims to the disclosed species (e.g., specifying APIDQ in dependent claim) can make a dependent claim commensurate with the specification even if the independent claim is too broad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dependent claim amendments to tie scope to disclosed embodiments; e.g., Amended Claim 2 limited to APIDQ was supported by the non-provisional specification and remedied scope issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worksheet procedure for examining written description support
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a stepwise worksheet: (1) determine BRI (and 112(f) invocation); (2) analyze whether each claim limitation has adequate written description support in the provisional; (3) analyze support in the non-provisional; (4) identify unsupported features. Order of provisional vs non-provisional analysis can vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which features are unsupported and prepare appropriate rejections/notifications. The workshop provides blank worksheet fields for each original and amended claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear examiner notification and sample rejection language
rubrics_metrics.description: When concluding lack of entitlement to a benefit or lack of written description, the examiner should use clear form paragraph language and indicate applicant options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the workshop include a sample Form Paragraph notifying lack of benefit (based on failure to comply with 112(a)) and sample rejections for lack of written description (7.30.01/7.31.01). Recommend options for applicant: cancel new matter, convert to CIP, or delete benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuations and divisionals follow same written-description-benefit rules as provisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: When a later application is a continuation or divisional, only those claims supported under 112(a) by the parent are entitled to the parent's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same analysis as for provisional-based benefit claims; see MPEP 211.05 for sufficiency of disclosure in prior-filed applications.
